notation.meaning: graph with node set \(V\) and edge set \(E\); every edge has a source and a target (the two ends of an undirected edge are interchangeable)
node-layers: a node \(v\) present in layer \(\alpha\)
adjacency matrix of the intra-layer edges of layer \(\alpha\)
coupling matrix of the inter-layer edges between layers \(\alpha\) and \(\beta\)
supra-adjacency matrix, of size \(n\,|L|\times n\,|L|\) when every node is present in every layer

formulas.name: Multilayer network (Kivela et al. 2014)
formulas.where: Node-layers \(V_M\) joined by edges \(E_M\); edges within one layer are intra-layer, edges between layers are inter-layer. A multiplex network is the case in which the inter-layer edges join only the copies of the same node.

formulas.name: Supra-adjacency matrix (De Domenico et al. 2013)
formulas.where: Block matrix of the layers on the diagonal and the couplings off the diagonal; the scalar \(\omega\) is the coupling weight of a multiplex network and is not fixed by the definition.

variants.multilayer: The structure and its supra-adjacency matrix; the coupling weight and which inter-layer edges exist are parameters of the model, not of the definition.

edge_cases.definition_gives: With no node-layers \(\mathcal A\) is the 0\(\times\)0 matrix; the definition allows it.
A node-layer with no intra- or inter-layer edge gives a zero row and column of \(\mathcal A\).
The coupling weight \(\omega\) is a free real parameter; the definition imposes no range, and measures built on \(\mathcal A\) may need \(\omega\ge 0\).

pn_centrality.note: The sources name the procedure (positive-negative centrality of signed ties) and list it in the documentation of a documented-only tool, but record no formula and no checkable primary source for it.

notation.meaning: graph with node set \(V\) and edge set \(E\); every edge has a source and a target (the two ends of an undirected edge are interchangeable)
a split of the nodes into two sets
partition of the nodes into \(k\) clusters
weight in \([0,1]\) between the two kinds of inconsistent edge

formulas.name: Balance (Harary 1953; Cartwright and Harary 1956)
formulas.latex: \prod_{e\in\text{cycle}}\sigma(e)=+1\ \text{for every cycle}\iff\exists X\subseteq V:\ \sigma(uv)=+1\text{ exactly when }u,v\text{ lie on the same side}
formulas.where: A signed graph is balanced when every cycle has an even number of negative edges; equivalently, the nodes split into two sets with positive edges inside and negative edges between.

formulas.name: Frustration index
formulas.latex: \ell(G)=\min_{X\subseteq V}\Bigl(\bigl|\{uv\in E^-:\ u,v\in X\text{ or }u,v\notin X\}\bigr|+\bigl|\{uv\in E^+:\ |\{u,v\}\cap X|=1\}\bigr|\Bigr)
formulas.where: Least number of edges whose sign must change (or that must be deleted) to reach balance; 0 exactly when the graph is balanced. The minimum is over all \(2^n\) splits. This is the two-group form of the partitioning criterion below.

formulas.name: Partitioning criterion (Doreian and Mrvar 1996)
formulas.latex: P_\alpha(C)=\alpha\,\bigl|\{uv\in E^-:\ u,v\text{ in the same cluster}\}\bigr|+(1-\alpha)\,\bigl|\{uv\in E^+:\ u,v\text{ in different clusters}\}\bigr|
formulas.where: Weighted count of negative ties inside clusters and positive ties between clusters, minimized over partitions into \(k\) clusters; \(k=2\) and \(\alpha=\tfrac12\) gives half the frustration objective.

variants.signed_balance: Three objects scored: the balance test (yes or no), the frustration index (a count of inconsistent edges, minimum over two-group splits) and the \(k\)-cluster partitioning criterion with weight \(\alpha\); a signed blockmodel is the partition that minimizes the criterion.

edge_cases.definition_gives: No cycle exists and no edge is inconsistent: balanced, frustration 0.

A positive loop is a balanced cycle of length 1; a negative loop is an unbalanced cycle that no split can repair, so the cycle form of the definition gives unbalanced while the split form ignores loops.
An edge of sign 0 has no sign in \(\{+1,-1\}\): the definition covers only signed edges, so such edges must be removed or assigned a sign first.
\(\alpha\) outside \([0,1]\) or \(k<1\) is outside the definition of the criterion.
